claim: VIX1D uses business years and business minutes (405-minute session), unlike VIX calendar time; weights shift from today's expiring strip to next day's strip through the session.
quote: The calculation of the VIX1D Index uses business years and business minutes – this is a different increment than the VIX Index, which uses calendar years and calendar minutes.
title: Cboe: What the VIX and VIX1D Indices Attempt to Measure

claim: Per VIX1D white paper (as reported by Cboe), when near-term expiry is under 60 business minutes away (~3:00pm ET), near-term vol is frozen at last valid value; VIX1D then mostly reflects next-day strip, so it is not a live read of the last hour.
quote: when the time to expiration for the near-term (current day expiry) series is less than 60 business minutes (approximately 3:00 p.m. ET), the single-term volatility of the near term will be the last valid value
title: Cboe: What the VIX and VIX1D Indices Attempt to Measure

claim: Retail SPX 0DTE long positions lost on average 53% of value (full sample) and 61% (since May 2022); short positions earned 48% and 56% (Beckmeyer, Branger, Gayda; retail trade data, after fees per summary).
quote: While the average long position of retail investors lost 53% of its value across the full sample and 61% for the sample since May 2022, selling insurance earned a large premium for the average trade, with returns of 48% and 56%, respectively.
title: WealthManagement: Retail Investors are in Love with Same Day Options (summary of Beckmeyer et al.)

claim: Vilkov (via secondary blog): SPX 0DTE VRP exists but is tiny (0.001% from 10am to close, Sep 2016-Jan 2024); straddles, condors, spreads, butterflies, risk reversals held to expiry showed no consistent profitability; only long-call/short-put risk reversal slightly positive (~0.01% of index, before costs).
quote: Only risk reversals - long call, short put - produced slightly positive mean returns, roughly 0.01% of the index value , trivial even before costs.
title: Breaking Nasdaq: The 0DTE illusion (summary of Vilkov)

claim: Hull Tactical summary of Vilkov: 0DTE options contain a VRP (implied above subsequently realised even at same-day horizons); differs in degree not kind from longer-dated; long 0DTE needs timing, direction and magnitude.
quote: implied volatility tends to be high relative to what is subsequently realized, even at same-day horizons.
title: Hull Tactical: 0DTE options, tiny edge, huge distribution

claim: SPY 0DTE options priced nearest $1.00, taken ~5 min before close on 2023-09-13: spread 5.8% vs ~1% for other expiries; ATM 0DTE penny spread 0.14/0.15 = 6.7% of mid vs 0.7% for next-day $1.43/$1.44 (single-day anecdote, Schaeffer's, self-reported).
quote: The spread on the 0DTE options (expiration date of Tuesday, Sept. 12) was 5.8%, while the spread on the options at other expirations were closer to 1%.
title: Schaeffer's: 0DTE Options: Are Higher Spreads Imminent?

claim: NDX 0DTE ATM options: expiring ITM options had mid-to-bid spread ~6 bps of spot, over double the average at close; with 25% slippage of mid-to-bid, round-trip annual cost 300-350 bps (Volos, self-reported, spread as fraction of spot not of option price).
quote: Expiring ITM call or put options on average have had high spreads of ~6 bps, over double the average spread at the market close across our full sample .
title: Volos: Improving 0-DTE Trading Returns By Avoiding Expensive Exits

claim: Cboe began listing up to two Monday and Wednesday expirations on qualifying single stocks (mkt cap > $700bn) and ETFs (AUM > $50bn) effective 2026-01-26; no daily (Tue/Thu) single-stock expiries confirmed.
quote: Effective January 26, 2026, the Cboe Options Exchanges will begin listing up to two Monday and Wednesday expirations for options on certain individual stocks or Exchange‑Traded Fund (ETF) Shares
title: Cboe notice: Options Exchanges to Begin Listing Options on Qualifying Securities

claim: Doshi, Pederzoli & Sert (May 2025 working paper): average percent effective spread of ATM (|delta| 0.375-0.625) SPX 0DTE options is 8.7% (calls) and 9.5% (puts), vs 6.2-6.3% for 1-6 DTE and about 2% for 42-48 DTE; LiveVol OPRA trades with NBBO, Jan 2004 - Jul 16 2021; effective spread = 2|ln P - ln M|, volume-weighted per day.
quote: The average spread is very high, ranging from a maximum of 9% for 0DTE options to a minimum of 2% for options with 21-48 days to maturity.
title: Risky Intraday Order Flow and Option Liquidity (Doshi, Pederzoli, Sert, May 23 2025)

claim: Option bid-ask spreads follow a U-shape over the trading day, widening at the open and close (Doshi, Pederzoli & Sert citing Cao, Jacobs & Ke 2024).
quote: bid-ask spread follows a U-shaped pattern over the trading day, widening at the open and close
title: Risky Intraday Order Flow and Option Liquidity (Doshi, Pederzoli, Sert, May 23 2025)
